topic: Massage during a busy, stressful season at work

slides.headline: End of quarter and your shoulders know it?
slides.sub: Where massage fits during a busy, stressful stretch at work.

slides.title: Stress shows up in your body
slides.body: Long hours, tight deadlines and less sleep often mean more clenching, shallow breathing and hours without moving. Many people feel it most in the neck, jaw and upper back.

slides.title: What massage can realistically do
slides.body: Remedial massage can help tight muscles feel easier and give your mind a break. It's a helpful support, not a replacement for sleep, movement and managing the workload itself.

slides.title: Book it before the crunch
slides.body: Put a session in the calendar at the start of a busy period rather than waiting until you're wrecked. Treat it like any other meeting you can't move.

slides.title: Pair it with small daily habits
slides.body: A ten-minute walk at lunch, a few slow breaths between meetings and a regular screen break can help the effects of a massage last longer.

slides.title: Check your extras cover
slides.body: If your extras cover includes remedial massage, you may be able to claim on the spot with HICAPS. Check your fund for any limits before you book.

slides.headline: Busy season on the horizon?
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physiotherapy work on the tension that builds up during demanding weeks at work.

caption:
Busy season at work tends to land in your neck and shoulders first.

Long hours, deadlines and less sleep often mean more clenching, shallow breathing and hours without moving. Remedial massage can help tight muscles feel easier and give your mind a break. It works well as a support alongside sleep, movement and a manageable workload, not as a replacement.

A simple tip: book your session at the start of a busy stretch, not the end. A short daily walk and regular screen breaks can help the effects last. If your extras cover includes remedial massage, you may be able to claim on the spot with HICAPS.

Book online via the link in bio.
